_scopes.feature_window: values[:origin], the whole observed history up to this decision's origin; every feature below is computed on it and recomputed from scratch at every decision
_scopes.serving_window: values[origin-192:origin], the last 192 points -- the only window the Consumer is given at serving time.  A feature computed over the whole history is not a feature of this window
_scopes.modified_region: what the chosen program actually changes on the serving window, against the linear-integrity baseline, decided at execution time.  No feature in this vocabulary measures it

task_kind.formula: the Task type of this decision

missing_fraction.denominator: number of points in the feature window

longest_missing_run_fraction.formula: length of the longest run of consecutive missing points, divided by values.size
longest_missing_run_fraction.denominator: number of points in the feature window

local_robust_z_peak.formula: max over the window of |filled - median| / scale, where median and scale are robust statistics of the same window
local_robust_z_peak.denominator: a robust scale of the feature window

estimated_region_start_fraction.formula: index of the first point of the union of the missing, outlier and level regions, divided by values.size
estimated_region_start_fraction.denominator: number of points in the feature window

estimated_region_end_fraction.formula: one past the last point of that same union, divided by values.size
estimated_region_end_fraction.denominator: number of points in the feature window

level_region_fraction.denominator: number of points in the feature window

level_region_end_fraction.formula: one past the last point of the level mask, divided by values.size
level_region_end_fraction.denominator: number of points in the feature window

outlier_region_end_fraction.formula: one past the last point of the expanded outlier region, divided by values.size
outlier_region_end_fraction.denominator: number of points in the feature window

post_shift_support_sufficient.computed_over: a fraction of the feature window, rescaled by the fixed constant 240
post_shift_support_sufficient.note: the 240 is a fixed downstream-window constant, not the feature window's own length

level_only_post_shift_support_sufficient.formula: the same test applied to level_region_end_fraction

level_excursion_score.formula: the level-candidate score of the window

estimated_level_offset.formula: median(filled[level_mask]) - reference, in the data's own units
estimated_level_offset.denominator: none; this is not a fraction

period_change_score.formula: period-change score from the period summary
period_change_score.computed_over: the feature window, after removing the level offset

period_reliability.formula: reliability term from the same period summary
period_reliability.computed_over: the feature window, after removing the level offset

period_evidence_status.formula: categorical status from the same period summary
period_evidence_status.computed_over: the feature window, after removing the level offset

imputation_probe_direction.computed_over: the fixed probe panel, not recomputed from the window

card.how_to_use_the_feature_semantics: each entry gives the formula and the window it is computed on.  Three scopes are different objects and the vocabulary only covers the first: the feature window is the whole observed history; the serving window is its last 192 points and is the only thing the Consumer sees; the modified region is whatever the program actually changes at execution time, and no feature here measures it.  A threshold you write is therefore a statement about the whole history, not about the window that will be served and not about the region that will be changed.  Nothing here tells you how a value moves from one window to the next -- that is not recorded and you should not assume it.

card.traceability_is_not_a_condition: series_uid and window_origin are here so you can trace a case back.  They are NOT part of the observable feature vocabulary and an applicability condition cannot name an entity, a dataset or a time position -- only the public features listed above.
card.what_you_may_write: Exactly one edit, on exactly one surface from writable_surface_catalog -- which now includes the body and the applicability condition of the guidance entry you wrote last time, so revising it in place is available and so is leaving it alone.  You are NOT required to add a new entry.  Say four things: (1) which facts on this card you are relying on; (2) what you now think the previous guidance got wrong or left out, as a hypothesis you accept may be wrong; (3) the one change; (4) what you expect to change in behaviour and effect, and what result would refute you.  Points (1) and (2) go in the text you write; (4) goes in predicted_agent_behavior_change, predicted_data_effect and falsification_condition.  Where the current behaviour works, say what should be kept.
what_you_may_not_write: the string 'Frozen program steps:' anywhere -- a fixed program handed to every sequence is exactly what this boundary excludes; Fast still forms and verifies each sequence's own program
candidate-supply authority, a serving scope, risk guards, verification rules, retrieval top_k or candidate slot counts
an applicability condition naming a series, a dataset or a course position

previous_guidance.this_text_is_already_in_the_snapshot: When forecast evidence shows both substantial missingness and a strong local robust deviation, inspect the missingness and deviation regions separately. Treat a broad or uncertain deviation span as insufficient public evidence for an outlier repair, because the observed negative cases include missing_fraction above 0.4 and local_robust_z_peak above 5 while the same mechanism also has mixed outcomes elsewhere. Prefer a minimal localized program only when the inspected hypothesis has a legal verifiable binding; otherwise retain identity. Keep the existing behavior for cases without this combined evidence and for narrowly localized deviations with sufficient public support.

proposal.written_text: When forecast evidence shows both substantial missingness and a strong local robust deviation, inspect the missingness and deviation regions separately before proposing or selecting a repair. The prior matched observations show that this guidance is retrieved reliably and is associated with more identity selections, but the delivered behavior can remain unchanged; therefore selection alone is not evidence that the repair was prevented. Treat a deviation as insufficiently actionable when its inspected region is broad or uncertain, or when no legal verifiable binding to the inspected hypothesis is available. In that case retain identity and do not let the combined feature condition itself justify an outlier program. When the deviation is narrowly localized and the inspection supplies a legal verifiable binding, preserve the existing exploration behavior: allow a minimal effect-distinct program candidate while leaving verification and Support to determine whether it is admissible. Keep existing behavior for cases without this combined evidence, and do not infer applicability from sequence identity, historical outcomes, or uninspected region geometry.
predicted_data_effect: For combined missingness and deviation contexts with broad or uncertain inspected deviation regions, identity should remain the selected control while no outlier repair is justified solely by the feature threshold.
For narrowly localized, legally bindable deviation hypotheses, the exploration candidate should remain available for verification rather than being suppressed by the guard.
The edit is expected to change selection and candidate ordering more often than the delivered program; a delivered repair should occur only when its public verification and Support remain admissible.
falsification_condition: In later matched forecast contexts satisfying the same public applicability condition, the revised guidance does not increase identity selection when inspection reports a broad or uncertain deviation region.
The revision suppresses exploration or retains identity despite a narrowly localized deviation hypothesis with a legal verifiable binding and consistently admissible public verification.
